range.label: Range
range.invalid_order: The start date must not be after the end date.

dashboard.savings_rate_sparkline_aria: Trailing 12-month savings rate over the last 24 months

tx.title: Transactions
tx.description: Browse, filter, and add household income and expenses.

banks.title: Banks
banks.settings_description: Connect a bank to sync movements into a review inbox. Nothing is added to your ledger until you confirm it.
banks.explain_sca: You'll be redirected to your bank to authenticate (SCA).
banks.explain_readonly: Only account movements are read — money can never be moved.
banks.explain_expiry: The permission expires in 90–180 days and will need re-linking.
banks.explain_selfhosted: Your data stays in this self-hosted instance.
banks.auto_sync_schedule: Automatic background sync runs daily at {{times}} (your time).
banks.label: Label
banks.status_credentials_required_hint: Paused: this household has no Enable Banking credentials. An owner can add them in the card above; syncing resumes automatically.
banks.status_credentials_mismatch_hint: This connection was authorized under a different Enable Banking application than the one configured. Re-link it to resume syncing.
banks.credentials_needed_notice: Linking a bank needs this household's Enable Banking credentials. An owner can configure them in the card above.
banks.credentials_description: The API application this household uses to talk to your banks. Each household configures its own; nothing is shared between them.
banks.credentials_key_configured: A private key is configured — leave blank to keep it
banks.credentials_key_not_configured: Paste the private key (PEM or base64)
banks.credentials_key_hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the current key.
banks.credentials_key_pkcs1: That looks like a PKCS#1 key (BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY). Convert it first: openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in key.pem -out key-pkcs8.pem
banks.credentials_key_file_loaded: Key loaded from {{name}} — save to store it.
banks.credentials_key_drop_hint: …or drop the downloaded key file here.
banks.credentials_key_file_too_large: That file is too large (max {{max}} KB). A private key file is only a few KB.
banks.credentials_key_file_binary: That file isn't readable as text. Upload the PEM/PKCS#8 private key, not a certificate bundle (.p12 / .pfx).
banks.credentials_key_file_empty: No key found in that file.
banks.credentials_redirect_hint: Register this exact URL in your Enable Banking application, or every link will be rejected.
banks.credentials_relink_warning: {{count}} existing connection(s) were authorized under a different application and will need re-linking.
banks.credentials_help_whitelist_body: In Restricted Production, Enable Banking only returns accounts explicitly linked to your application in the Control Panel, and any account that is not whitelisted is silently omitted — the connection will look active here but sync zero movements, with no error anywhere.
banks.credentials_help_identity: Syncing uses only the credentials saved here. Enter the same application id and key your connections were created with and they keep working; a different application requires re-linking each bank.
banks.credentials_help_encrypted: The private key is encrypted at rest and never shown again after saving.
banks.delete_confirm: Remove this connection and its pending movements?
banks.rules_description: Automatically suggest a category and direction for incoming movements. Confirming a movement whose counterparty no rule covers yet also remembers it as a learned rule.
banks.rules_page_description: Search, edit and prune the rules that pre-categorise incoming bank movements.
banks.rules_search_placeholder: Search by value, e.g. Albert Heijn
banks.delete_rules_confirm: Delete {{count}} selected rules? Already-confirmed movements are not affected.
banks.no_matching_rules: No rules match the current filters.
banks.truncated_note: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} — refine filters to see the rest
banks.callback_missing: Missing authorization details from the bank.
banks.replace_hint: The transaction you already recorded is updated in place with the bank's data — no second entry is created. Highlighted rows are what would change.
banks.replaced_toast: Transaction updated from the bank movement
banks.pick_candidate: {{count}} transactions match — pick the one to replace
banks.pick_candidate_hint: Pick a transaction above to compare it with this movement.
banks.candidate_bank_linked: already linked to a bank movement
banks.no_replaceable_match: There is no transaction left to replace — the match was deleted or already resolves another bank movement. You can still confirm this movement as a new transaction.
banks.fallback_needs_category: Pick a category on the row first to confirm it.
banks.split_hint: Divide this movement into parts that add up to its total exactly. Every part keeps the movement's date and direction, and can have its own category and description.
banks.split_nothing_left: Nothing left for this part — lower the other amount
banks.split_needs_category: Pick a category for this part
banks.credentials_help_step1: Sign in to the Enable Banking Control Panel and choose “Add a new application”:
banks.credentials_help_step2: Environment: choose Production — Sandbox only connects to test banks. You activate “Restricted Production” on it afterwards: real data, free, no eIDAS/TPP licence needed.
banks.credentials_help_step3: Key generation: choose “Generate in the browser (using SubtleCrypto) and export private key” — the key file then downloads automatically when you register. (“Generate outside the browser” is only for managing your own keys.)
banks.credentials_help_step5: Allowed redirect URLs: paste exactly this URL (use the Copy button above), one per line. A mismatch makes every bank link fail.
banks.credentials_help_step6: Description, data-protection email, privacy URL and terms URL are optional — leave them empty for personal use.
banks.credentials_help_step7: Press Register. Copy the application id into the field above; the downloaded key file is your private key — upload it or paste its contents, both work.
banks.credentials_help_step8_save: Save the credentials in this card (Save) and press “Validate credentials”.
banks.credentials_help_step8_gate: Do not continue to Phase B until validation succeeds.
banks.credentials_help_phase_a_title: Phase A — Create your Enable Banking application and save the credentials here
banks.credentials_help_phase_b_title: Phase B — Whitelist every bank account in the Control Panel
banks.credentials_help_b_step1: In the Control Panel, open your application, activate Restricted Production if you haven't yet, and use “Activate by linking accounts”.
banks.credentials_help_b_step2: Choose the bank the account belongs to.
banks.credentials_help_b_step3: The account holder authenticates with their own bank credentials (SCA). For a partner's or a relative's account, that person must do this step themselves — you cannot do it for them.
banks.credentials_help_b_step4: Repeat for EVERY account you intend to sync: each bank, each holder.
banks.credentials_help_b_gate: Do not link any bank in SharedLedger until every account you plan to sync appears as linked to the application in the Control Panel.
banks.credentials_help_phase_c_title: Phase C — Link your banks in SharedLedger
banks.credentials_help_c_step1: Only now, go to the Banks section below, pick the country and the bank, and link.
banks.credentials_help_c_step2: Each holder links their own account with their own SCA.
banks.credentials_help_c_symptom: If a connection shows active but 0 accounts, or never brings movements, the account was not whitelisted — go back to Phase B, whitelist it, then use Re-link on the connection.
banks.whitelist_check_title: Have you whitelisted this account in your Enable Banking application?
banks.whitelist_check_body: Non-whitelisted accounts link fine but sync nothing: the connection shows active, no movements ever arrive, and no error appears anywhere.

recurring.title: Recurring
recurring.description: Templates that automatically create transactions on a weekly, monthly, or yearly schedule.

budget.title: Budgets
budget.description: Set spending limits per category. Monthly applies to the selected month; annual spans the whole year.
budget.monthly_description: Spending limits for the selected month. The projection extrapolates current pace to month-end.

networth.title: Wealth
networth.snapshots_description: Point-in-time totals of every asset class and active liability. Take one whenever you want to track progress.
networth.movements_description: Contributions, withdrawals, and debt payments between snapshots. Used to attribute Wealth changes to flows versus market returns.
networth.flows_description: How your money moves: capital reallocations and cash adjustments.
networth.cash_no_adjustments: Add an adjustment to start tracking cash. Until then, cash carries over from the previous snapshot.
networth.cash_end_of_day_hint: The amount is taken as your cash at the end of the selected day. It will keep fluctuating afterwards based on the settings; only flows dated after it adjust the estimate.
networth.cash_breakdown: Since your last adjustment on {{date}} ({{amount}}), net flows {{net}} → estimated {{estimate}}.
networth.liabilities_description: Recurring debts (mortgage, loans, credit lines). Their balance is reflected in your Wealth snapshots, subtracted from your net worth. They are not linked to transactions — they neither create nor consume expenses. Inactive items are hidden from new snapshots.
networth.evolution_description: Wealth, assets, and liabilities plotted over time from your snapshots.
networth.allocation_description: Share of each asset class in your most recent snapshot.
networth.delta_warning: One or more values changed by more than 50%. Confirm to save.
networth.assets_description: Named things you own with a value (property, vehicles, valuables). Their value is reflected in your Wealth snapshots, added to your net worth. Each keeps its own dated value history. Inactive items are hidden from new snapshots.
networth.inactive_hint: Uncheck to mark sold/inactive — hidden from new snapshots.
networth.amortizable_balance_hint: Balance is computed from the loan schedule — open 📅 to manage it.
networth.loan_intro: A debt can contain one or more loans (e.g. a fixed-rate loan and a variable-rate loan). Its total balance and monthly instalment are the sum of the loans. Save a loan to compute its schedule.
networth.charge_day_hint: Day of the month the instalment is charged (1–31; a value past the month length uses the last day).
networth.no_parts: No loans yet. Add one to build the debt.
networth.charge_day_required: Charge day is required for a debt that contains loans.
networth.charged_empty: None yet — actual payments appear after the next charge day.
networth.start_mode_current_help: Enter the outstanding balance and its date; the schedule projects forward. Simple, exact balance, no past history.
networth.start_mode_origin_help: Enter the original principal and the loan's start date; the full schedule is generated from origin, including past payments. The current balance is computed.
networth.original_principal_help: The amount originally borrowed at the loan's start.
networth.origin_date_help: The loan's start date; the schedule is generated from here through the end.
networth.payment_history_hint: Payment rows are read-only. Correct via prepayment, rate revision or re-anchor.
networth.re_anchor_help: Set the real outstanding balance at a date; the schedule reprojects from there and keeps the past history.
networth.method_hint_interest_only: Interest only; the whole principal is due at the end.
networth.method_hint_zero: No interest; equal principal each month.
networth.outstanding_principal_help: The current outstanding balance of this loan — not the original amount borrowed.
networth.start_date_help: The date the outstanding balance is measured; the schedule projects forward from here (usually today).
networth.term_end_help: Enter either a term or an end date — each converts to the other.
networth.instalment_help: Or enter the instalment instead of a term; the term is computed.
networth.rate_revisions_help: Add a revision (date + new rate), including past dates; the schedule recalculates from each.
networth.prepayments_help: A one-off extra payment that reduces the debt. Reduce term keeps the instalment and finishes earlier; reduce instalment keeps the term and lowers the instalment.
networth.revaluation_explainer: Net worth minus cumulative contributions — the share attributable to market changes.
networth.no_movements_hint: Record Wealth movements to see how much of your growth came from contributions versus market changes.
networth.value_source_computed_hint: Auto-filled from your portfolio holdings valued at the snapshot date. Edit the value to override it.
networth.stale_prices_disclaimer: Some portfolio prices are stale or missing at this date; computed values use the last known price. You can override any value.
networth.auto_snapshot_description: Create Wealth snapshots on a schedule so tracking does not depend on remembering. Market classes are pre-filled from your portfolio; other classes are carried over from the previous snapshot for you to update.
networth.value_source_carried_over_hint: Carried over from the previous snapshot by an automatic snapshot. Edit it whenever it changes.

portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.description: Track individual crypto, ETF, stock and fund holdings with purchase lots. Prices come from market data providers.
portfolio.evolution_description: Market value of the portfolio over time, next to the remaining invested amount (drops when you sell).
portfolio.new_holding_hint: Type a symbol and pick a match to enable automatic prices. You can also create the holding unlinked and link it later.
portfolio.empty: No holdings yet. Create one to start tracking your investments.
portfolio.net_invested_tooltip: The money that actually left your pocket: {{open}} open cost − {{realized}} realized P&L. Buys funded by earlier sales cancel out, so sell-and-rebuy cycles don't count.
portfolio.net_invested_tooltip_house: You've taken back at least as much as you ever put in, so your current positions are funded entirely by realized gains ("house money"). {{open}} open cost − {{realized}} realized P&L.
portfolio.avg_cost_tooltip: Average purchase cost per unit = cost basis ÷ quantity
portfolio.net_invested_unavailable: You've taken back at least as much as you ever put in, so your current positions are funded entirely by realized gains ("house money"). There's no net invested to show a return over.
portfolio.cadence_tooltip: Crypto ~hourly; stocks, ETFs and exchange rates daily after market close; funds only via snapshots. Expand a holding to see its price date.
portfolio.label: Name
portfolio.stale_prices_warning: Some prices are stale or missing; values shown use the last known price.
portfolio.fund_no_provider: Funds have no automatic price provider yet.
portfolio.link_optional_hint: Optional: pick a match to fetch prices automatically. Skipping keeps the holding unlinked.
portfolio.roi_twr_description: Time-weighted return: chains the daily market returns between trades, so contributions and withdrawals are not counted as performance.
portfolio.xirr_explain: Annual growth rate of the money you put in, accounting for when you put it in. Computed from your {{flows}} buy/sell trades between {{from}} and {{to}}, each in EUR at its trade-date rate, plus the current value of open holdings ({{terminal}}) as a final inflow.
portfolio.xirr_explain_cumulative: Cumulative growth of the money you put in, accounting for when you put it in — the history is shorter than one year, so it is not annualized. Computed from your {{flows}} buy/sell trades between {{from}} and {{to}}, each in EUR at its trade-date rate, plus the current value of open holdings ({{terminal}}) as a final inflow.
portfolio.xirr_unavailable_unpriced: Some open holdings have no price, so the closing value is unknown.
portfolio.xirr_unavailable_not_computable: The cash flows admit no meaningful rate (e.g. no money has come back yet and the position is worthless, or everything happened on one day).
portfolio.benchmark_eur_note: Benchmarks are shown in EUR terms, converted at each day's ECB rate, and re-based to 0% at the start of the selected period.
portfolio.benchmark_partial_note: Some benchmarks only have data for part of this period; the missing start is left blank rather than estimated.

lendings.header_description: Money you lend to others — tracking only. Not counted toward your Wealth (a deliberate choice) and not linked to transactions.
lendings.confirm_settle: Mark this lending as settled? Interest will stop accruing.
lendings.confirm_write_off: Declare this lending written off? Interest stops accruing and it is excluded from outstanding totals.
lendings.home_note: Payments apply to interest first, then principal. These amounts are tracked separately from your Wealth.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.yoy_description: Compares income and expenses for the selected month across the last 5 years.
analytics.yby_description: Compares monthly expense totals across the selected years.
analytics.trailing_description: Income, expenses, and savings rate for the last 12 months ending this month.
analytics.forecast_description: Projects expenses for the next N months per category, using the chosen lookback window or active recurring templates.
analytics.horizon_help: Number of months to project ahead.
analytics.window_help: Lookback window (months) used to estimate per-category averages.
analytics.allocation_description: How income for the selected period was split across expense groups, with anything left over labelled as saved.
analytics.allocation_no_income: No income recorded for this period. The chart shows expenses only.
analytics.top_movers_description: Categories whose spending changed the most against the chosen baseline.
analytics.new_activity_description: Categories with spending this period but zero in the baseline.
analytics.totals_summary: Total increase across top 5: {{increase}}; total decrease: {{decrease}}
analytics.no_movers: No categories meet the baseline-and-period criteria.
analytics.recurring_share_description: Share of expenses that come from recurring transactions versus everything else, for the selected scope.
analytics.money_flow_description: Where money came from and where it went in the selected period. Income categories flow into the hub; the hub flows out to expenses, with the remainder saved.
analytics.money_flow_empty: No income or expenses in this period.
analytics.heatmap_description: Spending intensity per category across months. Color is scaled within each row so categories with different magnitudes are both readable.
analytics.cost_of_living_description: Essential monthly spend compared with total. Essentials are the structural floor of the household budget — costs that cannot be cut without materially changing how the household lives.
analytics.cost_of_living_no_data: No expenses in the selected range
analytics.explorer_description: Pick a single group or category and see how its spending behaves over time, with optional year-over-year overlay.
analytics.explorer_yoy_help: Overlay same period one year earlier
analytics.explorer_descriptions_hidden_for_group: Pick a single category to see its top descriptions.
analytics.stacked_description: Pick several groups and categories and see how much you spend across them and how it splits, month by month.
analytics.stacked_empty_selection: Select one or more groups or categories to build the chart.
analytics.daily_description: Calendar of daily spending. Click a day to see its transactions. Use the pattern range below to see how each weekday and day-of-month typically goes.
analytics.daily_calendar_empty: No spending recorded this month yet.
analytics.daily_pattern_dom_note: Days 29-31 may show lower averages because not every month reaches them.

fire.title: FIRE
fire.description: Financial Independence / Retire Early. Projects your investable assets toward your targets using Monte Carlo simulation, derived from your real data.
fire.settings_description: All FIRE parameters live here and persist for the household: targets, scenarios, contribution, inflation and taxes.
fire.target_year_effect: Simulations run from the latest snapshot up to this year.
fire.scenarios_help: Each scenario is a (mean, std dev) pair simulated via Monte Carlo. Add multiple to compare optimistic/pessimistic assumptions.
fire.scenarios_nominal_note: Returns are nominal; inflation is applied to the targets.
fire.add_historical_disabled: Available once your real return can be computed (record net worth movements).
fire.historical_tooltip: Derived from {{years}} year(s) of your own money-weighted returns — a statistically insufficient sample for forecasting; reference only.
fire.coast_explain: Coasting = the same Monte Carlo simulation with contributions stopped today (contribution = 0): the probability of reaching the tier's inflated target on time.
fire.table_explain: For each scenario and tier: the year the deterministic mean-return path crosses the target, the share of Monte Carlo trials that reach the target by the horizon, and the median crossing year among those that do.
fire.table_tax_note: Targets are gross of capital-gains tax: they cover the tax paid when selling to live.
fire.qualifying_help: Only balances in these classes count toward the FIRE targets.
fire.actual_return_explain: Money-weighted (XIRR) return of your qualifying classes between {{from}} and {{to}}: the first snapshot's value goes in, your {{movements}} recorded movement(s) flow in or out, and the latest snapshot's value comes back. Contributions count as capital, not as performance.
fire.actual_return_coverage_warning: may be overstated: {{months}} month(s) of history before your first recorded movement are not covered
fire.actual_return_gap_explain: Movements are only recorded from {{first}} — the {{months}} month(s) before that are not covered, so earlier growth is counted as return.
fire.no_return_no_movements: Record net worth movements to see your real return.
fire.no_return_insufficient_snapshots: At least two snapshots are needed to compute your real return.
fire.no_return_not_computable: Your real return could not be computed from the recorded data.
fire.tier_custom_base: your own figure, in today's money (it neither inflates nor grosses up)
fire.tier_lean_explain: Lean FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers your essential trailing-12 spending, the same base as the Cost of living tile) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.
fire.tier_fire_explain: FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers your total trailing-12 spending) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.
fire.tier_fat_explain: Fat FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers total spending × {{multiplier}}) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.
fire.tier_custom_explain: A wealth target you set yourself, treated as a nominal amount.
fire.tier_tax_note: Includes capital-gains tax: to spend {{net}} net you would withdraw {{gross}} (≈{{tax}} tax, {{rate}} effective).
fire.tier_months_note: Spending bases use {{months}} months of data (fewer than 12 available).
fire.tax_targets_note: Targets are gross of capital-gains tax, assuming {{gain}} of each withdrawal is realized gain.
fire.coverage_explain: Current coverage = qualifying wealth in the latest snapshot ({{wealth}}) ÷ target ({{target}}). Snapshots are the source of truth for wealth; the live portfolio value is not used.
fire.coverage_source_note: Coverage and projections start from the latest snapshot: {{value}} in qualifying classes as of {{date}}.
fire.no_spending_data: No spending data yet — record transactions to derive this tier.
fire.no_tiers_active: No target configured. Enable a tier or set a custom target in the settings below.
fire.owners_only: Only household owners can edit these settings.
fire.swr_effect: Annual share of your wealth you would withdraw once retired. At {{swr}}% your FIRE target is {{target}}; at {{alt}}% it would be {{altTarget}}.
fire.swr_effect_generic: Annual share of your wealth you would withdraw once retired. Lowering it raises every target.
fire.inflation_effect: Targets grow at this rate every year: the FIRE target becomes {{target}} in {{year}}.
fire.inflation_effect_generic: Targets grow at this rate every year; returns stay nominal.
fire.index_contribution_effect_on: The contribution rises {{inflation}}%/year, keeping its purchasing power.
fire.index_contribution_effect_off: A constant nominal contribution loses purchasing power every year, making long horizons look pessimistic.
fire.fat_multiplier_effect_generic: Fat FIRE assumes total spending times this factor.
fire.tier_toggles: Tiers shown in chart and table
fire.custom_target_help: Optional fourth tier: your own wealth target.
fire.contribution_savings_explain: Trailing-12 monthly average of income − expenses from your transactions.
fire.contribution_movements_explain: Trailing-12 monthly average of net contributions (contributions − withdrawals) into qualifying classes.
fire.contribution_missing_warning: The selected contribution source has no data yet: the projection runs without contributions until you pick another source or record data.
fire.contribution_gap: You save {{savings}}/month but invest {{movements}}/month — the difference stays out of the projection.
fire.nominal_note: All figures are nominal: returns are nominal and targets grow with {{inflation}}%/year inflation.
fire.tax_apply: Apply capital-gains tax to the projection
fire.tax_apply_effect: Targets rise to cover the tax on realized gains: to spend {{net}} net/year you would withdraw {{gross}} (≈{{tax}} tax).
fire.tax_apply_effect_generic: Targets rise to cover the tax on realized gains when selling to live.
fire.tax_brackets_help: Seeded with the Spanish scale (Ley 7/2024, FY 2025–2026). Brackets are data, not code: edit them here when the law changes.
fire.tax_brackets_invalid: Bounds must be non-negative numbers in strictly ascending order, rates between 0 and 100.
fire.tax_model_note: Only the gain share of each withdrawal is taxed (FIFO, per path in the simulation); loss offsetting is deliberately ignored — a conservative simplification. This is a planning estimate, not tax advice.
fire.gain_fraction_effect: Share of each withdrawal that is realized gain rather than principal; used only while your movements can't derive it.
fire.gain_fraction_movements: Currently derived from your movements: {{pct}}% of a withdrawal today would be gain.
fire.gain_fraction_manual: Manual fallback in use ({{pct}}%): record net worth movements to derive it from real data.
fire.spending_bases_help: Each tier's spending base is derived from your data by default; override it manually if your planning figure differs from reality. The derived value always stays visible.
fire.spending_essential_derived_explain: Trailing-12 monthly average of expenses in essential categories — the same base as the Cost of living tile.
fire.spending_total_derived_explain: Trailing-12 monthly average of all expenses.
fire.spending_essential_gap: Your real essential spending is {{derived}}/month; the projection uses your manual {{manual}}/month.
fire.spending_total_gap: Your real total spending is {{derived}}/month; the projection uses your manual {{manual}}/month.
fire.spending_coherence_warning: Essential spending exceeds total spending: Lean FIRE would exceed FIRE. Values are used exactly as entered — nothing is reordered or clamped.
fire.tier_lean_base_manual: based on your manual essential spending of {{monthly}}/month
fire.tier_fire_base_manual: based on your manual total spending of {{monthly}}/month
fire.tier_fat_base_manual: based on your manual total spending of {{monthly}}/month × {{multiplier}}
fire.tier_lean_explain_manual: Lean FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers your manual essential spending) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.
fire.tier_fire_explain_manual: FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers your manual total spending) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.
fire.tier_fat_explain_manual: Fat FIRE = annual withdrawal of {{annual}} (covers your manual total spending × {{multiplier}}) ÷ {{swr}}% SWR = {{target}}.

settings.title: Settings
settings.household_settings_description: Shared name, currency, and default language. Only owners can change these.
settings.members_list_description: People with access to this household.
settings.invitations_description: Generate invitation tokens to add owners or members. Share the resulting link with the person you want to invite.
settings.issued_token: Invitation token (copy this — it will not be shown again)
settings.wipe_description: Permanently delete all of this household's financial data — transactions, budgets and recurring templates, Wealth snapshots and movements, assets, liabilities and lendings, the investment portfolio, bank connections and their pending items, and notification/automation settings. This cannot be undone.
settings.wipe_warning: Everything in this household will be permanently removed: transactions, budgets, recurring templates, snapshots and movements, assets, liabilities and lendings, portfolio holdings and trades, bank connections, pending movements and categorization rules, and FIRE, notification and auto-snapshot settings. Only the household itself and its members are kept.
settings.households_description: Switch between households you belong to, set a default, or create a new one.
settings.create_household_description: Start a fresh household. You'll become its owner.
settings.delete_household_blocked: Cannot delete: this household is set as default by one or more members. They need to pick a different default first.
settings.delete_household_confirm: Permanently delete this household and everything in it (transactions, snapshots, budgets…)? This cannot be undone.
settings.custom_categories_description: Categories private to this household. Only the owner can create, edit, or delete them.
settings.delete_custom_category_warning: This will permanently delete the category and every transaction, budget, and recurring template using it. This cannot be undone.
settings.home_panels_description: Choose which panels appear at the top of your Home. This only affects your account — other household members keep their own layout.
settings.home_panels_disclaimer: Panels marked with ⓘ depend on data: even when switched on, they only appear once there is something to show. The monthly summary and the expenses chart are always shown.
settings.home_panel_data_dependent: This panel only appears when there is data to show. Turning it on won't display it while it has no data.
settings.portfolio_return_basis_description: How the return percentages (unrealized, realized and total) are worked out on your Home portfolio tile and the Portfolio page. This only affects your account and only the percentages, never the underlying amounts.
settings.portfolio_return_basis_help_OPEN_COST: Divides realized and total return by the cost of the positions you currently hold. Unrealized, realized and total then share one base and add up, so it reads like a normal buy-and-hold return.
settings.portfolio_return_basis_help_NET_INVESTED: Divides all three percentages by your net invested — the money you put in from outside (open cost minus realized profit), so buys funded by earlier sales cancel out. It's your own money currently at risk. Shows "—" if you've taken out more than you ever put in.
settings.portfolio_return_basis_help_TURNOVER: Divides realized return by the cost of every lot you have ever sold, and total return by that plus your open cost. Frequent selling and rebuying (common with crypto) inflates this base, so the percentages look small. This was the original behavior.
settings.portfolio_return_basis_disclaimer: For a return that accounts for when you put money in and took it out, see the XIRR figure on the Portfolio page.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Send a Telegram message to a chosen chat whenever data changes in this household. Only owners can configure this.
notifications.bot_token_configured: A token is configured — leave blank to keep it
notifications.bot_token_keep_hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the current token.
notifications.master_hint: Master switch. When off, no notifications are sent but the rest of the configuration is kept.
notifications.language_hint: Notifications are sent in the household's language.
notifications.test_ok: Test message sent — check your Telegram chat.
notifications.help_show: How do I get a bot token and chat ID?
notifications.help_step1_body: Open a chat with @BotFather, send /newbot, follow the prompts, and copy the token it gives you (looks like 123456789:AA…).
notifications.help_step2_title: 2. Add the bot to your chat
notifications.help_step2_body: For a private message, open your bot and press Start. For a group, add the bot as a member. For a channel, add it as an administrator so it can post.
notifications.help_step3_body: getUpdates only lists chats the bot has already heard from, so first send it a message: in a private chat press Start (or send /start); in a group, add the bot and then send any message. Now open the URL below (with your token) in a browser and read result[].message.chat.id. Group/channel IDs are negative.
notifications.help_step3_hint: Tip: bots like @userinfobot or @RawDataBot will also tell you a chat ID.

export.title: Export everything
export.description: Download a single ZIP containing transactions, recurring templates, movements, snapshots, lendings, and their payments — one CSV per dataset. The same files re-import cleanly.

import.title: Data import & export
import.settings_description: Import previously exported CSVs back into this household, or download a full backup as a ZIP.
import.page_description: Upload a CSV exported from this app. Validation runs first; nothing is written until you confirm.
import.transactions_description: Same format as Transactions → Export CSV. Duplicates of existing data are skipped automatically; rows duplicated within the same file are all imported with a numeric suffix appended to the description.
import.snapshots_description: Same format as Snapshots → Export CSV. Each date is one snapshot; choose what to do if a date already exists.
import.portfolio_description: One row per purchase lot; rows sharing asset_class and symbol become one holding. Duplicate lots are skipped.
import.movements_description: Same format as Movements → Export CSV. Duplicates of existing data are skipped automatically; rows duplicated within the same file are all imported with a numeric suffix appended to the description.
import.recurring_description: Same format as Recurring → Export CSV. Imports never advance the materialization clock — new templates fire from their start_date the next time you run them.
import.lendings_description: Same format as Lent → Export lendings CSV. Duplicates (same borrower, start date and principal) are skipped automatically.
import.lending_payments_description: Same format as Lent → Export payments CSV. Each row locates its lending by borrower and lending start date.
import.assets_description: Same format as Assets → Export CSV. Each asset is matched by name; value entries already present are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
import.liabilities_named_description: Same format as Liabilities → Export CSV. Each liability is matched by name; balance entries already present are skipped.
import.amortization_description: Rebuilds the schedules of amortizable liabilities: parts, rate revisions, prepayments and the generated instalments. Import liabilities first. Existing rows are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
import.duplicate_policy: If a date already has a snapshot
import.errors_truncated: Only the first 500 errors are shown.
import.skipped_found: {{count}} rows match existing data and will be skipped
import.adjusted_found: {{count}} rows are duplicated within the file — their descriptions will be tagged with (2), (3), … so each one stays unique

format.ai_hint: Tip: paste this whole reference into any AI assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, …) together with your bank statement, PDF account summary or other report, and ask it to produce a CSV that follows exactly this format. Then come back here, validate the result, and import it.

tx.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting (wrap a field in double quotes if it contains ;, " or a line break; escape " by doubling). First row is the literal header shown below; one transaction per data row. Amounts are always positive — the sign of the operation comes from the direction column.
tx.date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-25). The day the transaction occurred.
tx.direction: Either income or expense (lowercase). Must match the kind of the chosen category_code.
tx.category_code: One of the codes listed below. income.* codes are valid only with direction=income; the rest are expense.
tx.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator (e.g. 12,34); dot is also accepted on import. No thousand separators, no currency symbol. Up to 2 decimals are stored.
tx.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters. Leave the field empty if there is no description.
tx.created_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC (e.g. 2026-05-25T10:30:00Z). Defaults to now if empty.
tx.updated_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC. Defaults to now if empty.
tx.unknown_category_note: If a category_code in your CSV is not listed above, the row will be rejected. Create it first as a Custom category in Settings → Categories.
tx.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (date, direction, category_code, amount, description) match an existing transaction are skipped automatically.
tx.in_file_dedup: If the same row appears more than once within the file, every copy is imported. To keep each transaction distinct, “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … is appended to the description of the duplicates (or “(2)”, “(3)”, … if the description was empty). The preview lists every row whose description was changed before you confirm. Trade-off: once an identical row exists in the database, every later upload of that same row is skipped — even when it appears twice in the new file alongside the existing one. To add a genuine second copy, give it a distinct description or delete the existing row first.

snap.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below. A Wealth snapshot on a given date is built by grouping rows that share the same date. Each snapshot must include a value row for every asset class AND for every active liability of the household, otherwise the whole date is rejected.
snap.date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. All rows with the same date form one snapshot.
snap.note: Optional free text. Must be identical on every row for the same date (otherwise the date is rejected).
snap.kind: Either asset or liability (lowercase). Determines what key is expected on this row.
snap.key: If kind=asset: one of the asset class codes below. If kind=liability: the exact name of an active liability defined in this household (case-sensitive).
snap.value: Non-negative decimal (0 is allowed). Comma is the canonical decimal separator; dot is also accepted on import.
snap.asset_codes_note: Asset class codes are predefined and cannot be customized. Rows referencing a code that is not listed above will be rejected.
snap.liabilities_note: Liability rows must reference the exact name of a liability that already exists and is active in this household. Inactive or unknown names will be rejected. Create or activate liabilities in Wealth → Liabilities first.
snap.no_liabilities: No active liabilities in this household yet.
snap.rules: Per-date rules: every asset class must have exactly one value row, every active liability must have exactly one value row, and no asset/liability key may repeat within the same date.

rec.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below; one recurring template per data row. Imports do not advance the materialization clock — newly imported templates fire from their start_date the next time you run them.
rec.direction: Either income or expense (lowercase). Must match the kind of the chosen category_code.
rec.category_code: One of the codes listed below.
rec.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator (e.g. 45,00); dot is also accepted on import. Up to 2 decimals are stored.
rec.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
rec.cadence: One of weekly, monthly, or yearly (lowercase). Determines which of the day/month columns is required.
rec.day_of_week: 1-7 (1=Monday … 7=Sunday). Required when cadence=weekly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.day_of_month: 1-31. Required when cadence=monthly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.month_of_year: 1-12. Required when cadence=yearly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.day_of_month_yearly: 1-31. Required when cadence=yearly. Must be empty otherwise.
rec.start_date: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. The earliest date this template can fire.
rec.end_date: Optional ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. The template stops firing after this date. Must be ≥ start_date.
rec.active: true or false. Inactive templates are kept but never fire automatically.
rec.dedup: Duplicate detection: a row is skipped automatically if every column matches an existing template (direction, category, amount, cadence, all day/month fields, start/end dates, active, and description).
rec.in_file_dedup: If two rows inside the file are identical in every column, the duplicates get “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … appended to their description so each one stays distinct.

mov.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) as decimal mark, RFC-4180 quoting. First row is the literal header shown below; one movement per data row. Movements record contributions or withdrawals against an asset class, or payments against a liability — they do not affect transaction totals.
mov.type: One of contribution, withdrawal, or debt_payment (lowercase).
mov.asset_class_code: Required when type is contribution or withdrawal — one of the asset class codes below. Must be empty when type=debt_payment.
mov.liability_name: Required when type=debt_payment — exact name of an existing active liability in this household. Must be empty when type is contribution or withdrawal.
mov.amount: Positive decimal. Comma is the canonical decimal separator; dot is also accepted on import. No sign — the type column determines the effect.
mov.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
mov.created_at: Optional ISO instant in UTC (e.g. 2026-05-25T10:30:00Z). Defaults to now if empty.
mov.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (date, type, target, amount, description) match an existing movement are skipped automatically. target is the asset_class_code or the liability.
mov.in_file_dedup: If the same row appears more than once within the file, every copy is imported. To keep each movement distinct, “ (2)”, “ (3)”, … is appended to the description of the duplicates (or “(2)”, “(3)”, … if the description was empty). The preview lists every row whose description was changed before you confirm. Trade-off: once an identical row exists in the database, every later upload of that same row is skipped — even when it appears twice in the new file alongside the existing one. To add a genuine second copy, give it a distinct description or delete the existing row first.

lending.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) decimal, RFC-4180 quoting, ISO dates. The first row is the literal header; one lending per row. Amounts are always positive.
lending.borrower_name: Free text. Name of the person you lent to.
lending.principal_amount: Positive decimal. Amount lent, in the household currency.
lending.start_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Date the money was lent.
lending.annual_interest_rate: Decimal in percentage points (e.g. 5,00 = 5%). Required when interest_type is simple or compound; empty otherwise.
lending.compounding_period: monthly or yearly. Required when interest_type=compound; empty otherwise.
lending.description: Optional free text up to 500 characters.
lending.status: active, settled or written_off. Optional; defaults to active.
lending.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (borrower_name, start_date, principal_amount) match an existing lending are skipped automatically.

lending_payment.intro: European-CSV dialect: UTF-8, semicolon (;) column separator, comma (,) decimal, ISO dates. The first row is the literal header; one payment per row. Amounts are always positive.
lending_payment.borrower_name: Must match an existing lending's borrower_name.
lending_payment.lending_start_date: Must match that lending's start_date; together with the borrower it locates the lending.
lending_payment.payment_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of the payment received.
lending_payment.matching_note: If multiple lendings match the (borrower_name, loan_start_date) tuple, the row is rejected as ambiguous.
lending_payment.dedup: Duplicate detection: rows whose (borrower_name, loan_start_date, payment_date, amount, description) match an existing payment are skipped automatically.

portfolio.intro: One row per trade (BUY or SELL). Rows that share asset_class and symbol belong to the same holding, which is created automatically. Net quantity, remaining cost basis and realized P&L are computed by replaying the trades (FIFO). For pricing, the easiest path is to import first and then link each holding from the app using its search — leave provider and provider_symbol blank. Those columns exist mainly so an export keeps its links on re-import.
portfolio.asset_class: One of crypto, etf, stock, fund.
portfolio.symbol: Your identifier for the holding (e.g. BTC, WEBN, AAPL). Uppercased automatically.
portfolio.label: Display name for the holding; taken from the first row.
portfolio.native_currency: ISO 4217 currency the instrument trades in. Defaults to EUR.
portfolio.isin: Optional 12-character ISIN; used to auto-link stocks/ETFs. Leave blank for crypto.
portfolio.provider: Optional price source: coingecko, yahoo, eodhd or twelvedata. Best left blank: after importing, open the holding and use the in-app search to link it — that finds the exact provider symbol for you. Only fill these in if you already know the precise identifiers.
portfolio.provider_symbol: The holding's exact identifier at that provider (e.g. bitcoin for CoinGecko, WEBN.DE for Yahoo). Required whenever provider is set. Hard to guess by hand — prefer linking after import via search.
portfolio.quantity: Units bought; positive, comma decimal, up to 12 decimals.
portfolio.unit_price: Price per unit in cost_currency (purchase price for BUY, sale price for SELL); comma decimal.
portfolio.cost_currency: Currency of unit_price and fee. Defaults to native_currency.
portfolio.fee: Optional trade fee in cost_currency (added to cost on BUY, subtracted from proceeds on SELL).
portfolio.type: BUY or SELL. Empty defaults to BUY.
portfolio.grouping: Multiple trades of one holding = multiple rows with the same asset_class and symbol. Sells must be covered by earlier buys.
portfolio.dedup: Rows matching an existing trade on type, asset class, symbol, date, quantity, unit price and currency are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
portfolio.note: Optional free-text note for the trade, up to 500 characters. Not part of the duplicate check.

assets.intro: One asset per name, with zero or more dated value rows. Repeat the name on each value row; leave value_date and value empty to import an asset with no history yet.
assets.name: Asset name; identifies the asset (reused if it already exists).
assets.active: true or false. Inactive assets are excluded from new snapshots.
assets.value_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of a value observation. Optional.
assets.value: Value on that date; comma decimal. Required when value_date is set.
assets.dedup: A value row already present (same date and value) is skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.

liab.intro: One liability per name, with zero or more dated balance rows. Amortizable liabilities carry their schedule separately (Amortization import); leave their balance rows empty here.
liab.name: Liability name; identifies the liability (reused if it already exists).
liab.active: true or false. Inactive liabilities are excluded from new snapshots.
liab.amortizable: true when the balance is computed by an amortization schedule.
liab.charge_day: For amortizable liabilities, day of month (1–31) the instalment is charged.
liab.balance_date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD of a manual balance. Optional (empty for amortizable).
liab.balance: Balance on that date; comma decimal. Required when balance_date is set.
liab.dedup: A balance row already present (same date and value) is skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.

amort.intro: Rebuilds the schedules of amortizable liabilities. Each row is one record: a part, a rate revision, a prepayment, or a generated instalment (entry). The liability must already exist and part rows must precede their revisions/prepayments/entries.
amort.liability_name: Name of an existing amortizable liability.
amort.part_label: Identifies the part within the liability; keep it stable across a part's rows.
amort.record_type: One of part, revision, prepayment, entry.
amort.date: ISO YYYY-MM-DD: start date (part), effective date (revision), date (prepayment), charge date (entry).
amort.fields: Remaining columns are used per record type: part → method, principal, annual_rate, term_months, instalment, start_mode, anchor_date, anchor_balance; revision → annual_rate; prepayment → amount, mode; entry → principal, interest, resulting_balance.
amort.dedup: Existing parts (by start date, principal and method), revisions, prepayments and entries are skipped, so re-importing an export is safe.
